sections.title: 1. Select a room and its participants
2. Open the room and continue
Show how each character responds (optional)
sections.markdown:
## Show how each character responds (optional)

Every saved turn includes `characters`, one entry per cast member, so your app can change a portrait or show an empty seat. Using them is optional; nothing else depends on them.

- `presence` is `present`, `stepped_away` or `left`. Characters can step out and return, and someone pushed too far can leave for the rest of the session.
- `expression_group` is the simpler set: `steady_and_engaged`, `more_open`, `more_careful`, `more_strained` or `participating_less`. Five portraits per character are enough.
- `expression` is the detailed state, one of 16, for finer portraits. Each belongs to one group, listed in the OpenAPI.

Both are `null` when no expression was reported, including during a safety moment: show the neutral portrait. These are simulated cast responses, not a reading of a real person. Show them as faces or cues rather than labels, so your users practice reading people.

sections.title: 3. Return to saved practice
sections.markdown:
## 3. Return to saved practice

Read the session, paged playback, debrief and cross-session insights under `/v1/conversation`. These reads make no new generation purchase. Use the returned cursor to continue playback. Debrief becomes available when the practice closes.

Every saved turn includes stable speaker identities, its original controls and explicit structure availability. When attribution is unavailable, show the saved text without inventing a speaker. Debriefs describe the recorded practice, its conditions and the moments that mattered.

sections.title: 4. Add optional whole-turn audio
sections.markdown:
## 4. Add optional whole-turn audio

The audio contract accepts a saved session and turn, never arbitrary text. `POST /v1/conversation/voice` with `operation: "generate"` creates one generation covering participating cast and Coach. A retry retrieves the same saved or pending generation.

A `202` response means the generation is pending. Save its `audio_id`. To continue, send `POST /v1/conversation/audio/AUDIO_ID/continue` with the same user and assignment, using a key with `chat` and `sessions:read` scopes. Respect `Retry-After`. Each request advances at most one segment of that existing purchase. Stop on a terminal status; a failed generation has no audio charge.

Find existing generations with `GET /v1/conversation/sessions/SESSION_ID/audio`, following its pagination cursor. `GET /v1/conversation/audio/AUDIO_ID` reads current status. Neither read creates or continues speech generation.

Fetch saved segment URLs through your authenticated server. Audio expires 24 hours after creation; playback does not extend that time or synthesize again. A segment fetched after expiry returns `410` `AUDIO_EXPIRED`. Use explicit `regenerate`, a new operation key and `replaces_audio_id` for a new purchase.

sections.title: 5. Provide export and deletion
sections.markdown:
## 5. Provide export and deletion

Export paged saved turns, setup, consent, preferences, practice summaries and audio-generation metadata with `POST /v1/conversation/data/export`. Export requires its dedicated key scope. Download available recordings through their authenticated audio routes before expiry. Session deletion also removes session-derived memory and saved audio. End-user erasure covers the user’s practice data; content-free financial records remain.

Deletion immediately revokes content access. A `202` receipt with `status: "pending"` means private audio cleanup is not yet confirmed. Retry the same deletion with its original `operation_id` until the receipt says `completed`.

Text retention is 180 days since activity in live mode and 30 days in test mode. Reads do not renew retention. Audio always uses its separate 24-hour creation clock.

## Contract downloads

[OpenAPI](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/openapi/conversation.openapi.json) · [Request, event and resource schemas](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/openapi/schemas/conversation-v1.schema.json)

Runnable server examples: [TypeScript](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/examples/conversation/conversation.ts) · [Python](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/examples/conversation/conversation.py) · [cURL](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/examples/conversation/conversation.sh) · [Complete workflow and recovery guide](https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/examples/conversation/README.md).

Each example sends one explicit request from a saved intent, and each has offline tests. Run them free on a test assignment; add live access when you are ready.

The v1 request envelope supports 1–5 participants, 10,000 learner characters per turn and at most 100 rows per read. Every workspace includes fifty free text attempts. Your workspace shows its current rate. Request and concurrency limits apply across keys.

Keep the assigned release and returned request ID when contacting [developer support](mailto:developers@foreverlearning.ai). Saved sessions retain their original release and rate.

sections.title: One price for the whole turn.
sections.markdown:
## One price for the whole turn.

| Usage | Price | Includes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text | $0.03 per billable turn | Participating cast and Coach |
| Optional audio | +$0.05 per spoken turn | All participating voices and spoken coaching |
| Text with audio | $0.08 total | One text turn and one saved audio generation |

Ten billable text turns cost $0.30. With newly generated audio for each turn, the total is $0.80. The opening and the closeout are billable turns. The number of participants does not add a per-speaker fee. Fifty free text attempts in every workspace.

Creating an empty room and reading saved conversations, debriefs and insights do not add a generation charge. Text opening and ordinary turns bill at dispatch, with the existing refund for an observed failure before content. Generated closeout bills when saved.

Audio bills once the complete turn audio is successfully saved. Replay is free for 24 hours from creation, with earlier removal when the session or user data is deleted. Regeneration is an explicit new purchase. Audio requires available balance.

Review the rate and the free test attempts in your workspace before adding the API. These prices do not change any existing workspace assignment.

examples.text:
# Conversations API integration examples

These clients cover the full Conversations API contract. They make **one explicitly
selected request per invocation**, with no automatic retries, voice purchases or
continuations. Add the Conversations API to your workspace in the console and
create a scoped server key before you run them; a request on a live assignment is
a purchase at your workspace's rate.

Test mode grants 50 lifetime attempts per workspace and stable Conversations listing,
shared across members and keys, at no charge. A generated opening, each reply and the
closeout debrief count, and a dispatched attempt counts even if it fails; the internal
output retry and an exact replay do not. A test assignment keeps the allowance of the
publication it was enrolled on; the console shows that figure and what remains. Test
mode is text only: audio needs a live assignment and balance. Reserve an attempt for
closeout. Exhaustion never silently switches to live charging.

Use Node 24+ for `conversation.ts`, Python 3.11+ for `conversation.py`, or Bash/Git
Bash with cURL and jq for `conversation.sh`. Each client has offline tests.

Store the API key in the server environment as `FOREVERLEARNING_API_KEY`. Never
put it in a request file, browser, command-line argument, source repository or log.
Use a private local directory for request/response files: they can contain learner
content. On Windows, use your user-owned directory and its access controls.

## Save the intent before dispatch

Every request file fixes the assigned host, assignment and pseudonymous user, so
a retry cannot silently move to another environment or user. Replace these
placeholders with your approved assignment. Generate a UUID **once per new
mutation**, persist it, and retain that same ID and body on retries. A new user
action gets a new file and UUID. For lifecycle bodies, use that UUID as the
`operation_id` too.

```json
{
  "base_url": "https://ASSIGNED-API-HOST/v1",
  "assignment_id": "ASSIGNED-UUID",
  "external_user_id": "synthetic-practice-user",
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/conversation/catalog"
}
```

```sh
node conversation.ts catalog.request.json catalog.response.json
python conversation.py catalog.request.json catalog.response.json
bash conversation.sh catalog.request.json catalog-response-directory
```

Choose one client; do not run all three commands as three purchases. Each output
must be new. An empty/partial output after failure is not a completed receipt.
Recover with the unchanged request file and a new output destination. TypeScript
and Python return `{status, retry_after, data}` for JSON/SSE; audio downloads are
raw MP3 bytes. cURL saves headers, HTTP status and raw bytes. For cURL SSE, use
`parse_stream` from `conversation.py` to verify the complete stream before acting:

```sh
python -c 'from pathlib import Path; from conversation import parse_stream; print(parse_stream(Path("opening-response/response.raw").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["request_id"])'
```

For closeout, pass `True` as `parse_stream`'s second argument. No `[DONE]` sentinel
is used. HTTP 200 and provisional text alone do not establish successful billing
or saved content. The clients verify stream/session/receipt identity and safety
presence, preserve the final receipt, and refuse truncated completion.

## Complete practice flow

Keep the scope fields above in each file. These are the remaining fields/bodies;
replace IDs with catalog or prior-response values. Key scopes are cumulative:
`chat` for mutations, `sessions:read` for saved reads and audio continuation,
`data:export` for export, `data:erase` for user erasure.

| Step | Method and path | Body or query | Cost / completion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Catalog | `GET /conversation/catalog` | No body | Free; select actual room/persona IDs. |
| Prepare | `POST /conversation/sessions` | Setup example below | Free; persist `session_id` and `content_release`. |
| Opening | `POST /chat` | `{"session_id":"SESSION","conversation":{"operation":"opening"}}` | $0.03 at dispatch; no learner prompt. |
| Ordinary turn | `POST /chat` | Turn example below | $0.03 at dispatch, subject to observed-precontent refund. |
| Recover | `GET /requests/REQUEST_ID` | No body | No new generation; wait for committed outcome or retry exact original POST. |
| Read consent | `GET /conversation/sessions/SESSION/consent` | No body | Free. |
| Change consent | `POST /conversation/sessions/SESSION/consent` | `{"action":"soften"}` | Explicit revision; use the documented action enum. |
| Reopen | `GET /conversation/sessions/SESSION` | No body | Saved scope, state and current controls. |
| Playback | `GET /conversation/sessions/SESSION/playback` | `"query":{"limit":25}` | Free; follow `next_cursor`. |
| Close | `POST /sessions/SESSION/end` | `{"operation_id":"SAVED-UUID"}` | Billable generated closeout on commit; require `session_ended`. |
| Debrief | `GET /conversation/sessions/SESSION/debrief` | No body | Free; observe availability, without inventing a score. |
| Insights | `GET /conversation/insights` | No body | Free; recorded practice, not diagnoses. |
| Session list | `GET /conversation/sessions` | `"query":{"limit":25}` | Follow every opaque cursor without changing scope. |

A learner has one active session at a time. Opening the learner's next session first
closes the open one with a generated closeout, charged as a closeout ($0.03, or one
attempt in test mode), the same as calling `end`. Calling `end` is optional; call it
when you want the debrief ready before the learner's next session.

An authored setup body:

```json
{"setup":{"kind":"room","room_id":"CATALOG-ROOM","mode":"guided","participants":[{"persona_id":"CATALOG-PERSONA"}]},"controls":{"cast_language":"en-US","cast_speech":"natural","challenge":"supportive","emotional_heat":"calm"}}
```

Open practice uses `{"kind":"open","mode":"open_practice","cast_shape":"one_on_one","participants":[...] ,"topic":"A fictional team handoff"}`.
For multiple participants, choose `cast_shape:"room"`; use one to five supported
personas and the catalog's room constraints. Topic/intensive consent is explicit;
see the schemas before choosing a sensitive scenario. The practice type determines
which setup fields are accepted. Do not send consumer/private prompt documents.

An ordinary turn body:

```json
{"session_id":"SESSION","prompt":"What would help us agree on the next step?","conversation":{"operation":"turn","controls":{"challenge":"realistic","emotional_heat":"calm"}}}
```

Omitted controls retain the last saved value. The five controls are cast language,
speech style, challenge, emotional heat and coaching lens. Coach ordinarily uses
English. No fixed session turn cap applies. Request and output bounds are enforced
server-side; your workspace shows its current rate, and request and concurrency
limits apply across keys.
Emotional heat `raw` is accepted in turn controls only, as the end user's own choice.

Each `conversation_turn` carries `characters`: per cast member, `expression` (16
states), `expression_group` (five codes, the simpler set) and `presence`. They are
optional to use, for portraits or seat state; see `CONVERSATION_API.md`.

## Optional whole-turn audio

1. Explicitly request `POST /conversation/voice` with
   `{"session_id":"SESSION","turn_id":"SAVED-TURN","operation":"generate"}`.
   Persist the returned `audio_id` and original request. Only saved cast/Coach text
   can be spoken; arbitrary TTS text is not accepted.
2. On status 202/pending, respect `Retry-After`. Each explicit
   `POST /conversation/audio/AUDIO/continue` with `{}` advances at most one segment
   of the existing purchase. Do not call `voice` again with a new purchase ID to
   recover a pending generation. Stop on ready, failed or expired.
3. Read `GET /conversation/audio/AUDIO`, or discover generations using
   `GET /conversation/sessions/SESSION/audio` and its pagination cursor. Reads do
   not continue generation. Fetch a returned segment only through its authenticated
   `/conversation/audio/AUDIO/segments/SEGMENT` path on the same assigned API host.
4. The whole successful saved generation costs $0.05, including every participating
   voice and spoken Coach. Replay is free for 24 hours from creation, with earlier
   deletion. Balance is required; there is no audio grace. A failed generation has
   no audio customer charge. Internal characters do not change the customer unit.
5. Explicit regeneration uses a **new** saved intent and
   `{"session_id":"SESSION","turn_id":"SAVED-TURN","operation":"regenerate","replaces_audio_id":"AUDIO"}`.
   That is a new purchase. Text plus one successful audio generation totals $0.08.

## Privacy and deletion

`POST /conversation/data/export` uses an empty body and `"query":{"limit":25}`.
Follow `next_cursor` in subsequent query parameters until null, preserving scope.
Do not put `operation_id` or pagination in its body. Each
page returns saved setup, turns, preferences, consent, practice memory and audio
metadata; download still-available audio separately before its expiry.

`DELETE /sessions/SESSION` with `{"operation_id":"SAVED-UUID"}` deletes a session.
`POST /data/erase` with the same body shape erases the scoped API user's practice
data. These are explicit destructive choices, separate from closeout. Content
access is revoked immediately; a pending 202 receipt means audio cleanup is not
confirmed. Retry the identical lifecycle operation until `status:"completed"`.
Financial records remain. Live text retention is 180 days since activity; test
retention is 30 days. Reads do not extend retention; audio uses its own fixed clock.

The console's Sandbox namespace is separate from these API examples. Never add an
operator's internal namespace prefix to an API end-user identifier.

## Errors and support

401/403 require correcting identity, assignment or scope; 402 concerns balance or
budget; 409 can mean pending work or a stale revision; 422 can mean reused
idempotency identity with changed input; 429 requires the supplied retry guidance.
An unavailable or interrupted response remains uncertain. Resolve the original
request before a fresh purchase. Do not add automatic provider retries.

Keep the assigned release and the returned request ID when contacting developer
support at developers@foreverlearning.ai. Saved sessions retain their original
release and rate.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# cURL + jq, Bash/Git Bash. Exactly one request, no redirects/retries.
# bash conversation.sh saved-request.json NEW-private-response-directory
set -euo pipefail
umask 077
[[ $# == 2 ]] || { echo 'Usage: bash conversation.sh saved-request.json NEW-response-directory' >&2; exit 2; }
intent=$1
destination=$2
base=$(jq -er '.base_url' "$intent")
path=$(jq -er '.path' "$intent")
method=$(jq -er '.method' "$intent")
assignment=$(jq -er '.assignment_id' "$intent")
subject=$(jq -er '.external_user_id' "$intent")
operation=$(jq -r '.idempotency_key // ""' "$intent")
[[ $base =~ ^https://[A-Za-z0-9.-]+(:[0-9]+)?/v1/?$ ]] || { echo 'Invalid API base' >&2; exit 2; }
[[ $path =~ ^/(chat|requests/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+|sessions(/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(/(end|discard|history))?)?|session/status|data/(export|erase)|conversation/(catalog|insights|voice|data/export|sessions(/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(/(consent|playback|debrief|audio))?)?|audio/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(/(continue|segments/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+))?))$ ]] || { echo 'Invalid API path' >&2; exit 2; }
uuid='^[a-f0-9]{8}(-[a-f0-9]{4}){3}-[a-f0-9]{12}$'
[[ $assignment =~ $uuid && $method =~ ^(GET|POST|DELETE)$ ]] || exit 2
[[ -n $subject && ${#subject} -le 200 && $subject != *$'\n'* && $subject != *$'\r'* ]] || exit 2
[[ ${FOREVERLEARNING_API_KEY:-} =~ ^[[:graph:]]{1,512}$ ]] || { echo 'Set the server-held key in FOREVERLEARNING_API_KEY' >&2; exit 2; }
[[ $method == GET || $operation =~ $uuid ]] || { echo 'Save an operation UUID first' >&2; exit 2; }
jq -e '(.query // {}) | keys | all(. == "limit" or . == "cursor" or . == "session_id")' "$intent" >/dev/null
query=$(jq -r '(.query // {}) | to_entries | map((.key|@uri)+"="+(.value|tostring|@uri)) | join("&")' "$intent")
url=${base%/}$path
[[ -z $query ]] || url=$url?$query
# Reserve the entire output directory before any request; never overwrite a receipt.
mkdir -- "$destination"
headers=$destination/request-headers.private
trap 'rm -f -- "$headers"' EXIT
printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s\nX-Assignment-Id: %s\nX-User-Id: %s\n' "$FOREVERLEARNING_API_KEY" "$assignment" "$subject" >"$headers"
args=(--silent --show-error --proto '=https' --max-time 120 --max-filesize 8388608 --request "$method" --header "@$headers"
  --dump-header "$destination/response.headers" --output "$destination/response.raw" --write-out '%{http_code}')
if [[ $method != GET ]]; then
  printf 'Content-Type: application/json\nIdempotency-Key: %s\n' "$operation" >>"$headers"
  jq -c '.body // {}' "$intent" >"$destination/request-body.private"
  [[ $(wc -c <"$destination/request-body.private") -le 49152 ]] || exit 2
  args+=(--data-binary "@$destination/request-body.private")
fi
# A nonzero curl result or an error frame is ambiguous, even if some text arrived.
curl "${args[@]}" --url "$url" >"$destination/http-status"
status=$(cat "$destination/http-status")
[[ $status =~ ^2[0-9][0-9]$ ]] || { echo "HTTP $status; retain the saved request and inspect its request ID" >&2; exit 1; }
echo 'Transport finished. Verify JSON status or the final SSE receipt before another operation.'

kits.prompt:
Goal: a practice page where a user rehearses a hard conversation with a character from the Conversations API, and sees the Coach's note beside the scene.

Read first: https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/conversation-practice/ (the Conversations API integration guide), and the OpenAPI contract and the TypeScript example linked there. Use only what they describe.

Start from: an empty folder.

Build, in TypeScript on Node 24 or later:
1. A small server that holds the key and is the only part that calls the Conversations API. Give each new browser a pseudonymous user id, kept in a cookie, and send it as X-User-Id.
2. The first time a user opens the page, read the catalog, find the ready-made room titled "Direct Feedback To A Report", and prepare one session for that user in guided mode, with the first persona the room recommends. Keep the session id on the server for that user, and request the room's opening once for that session.
3. Show the opening. Then send each message the user types as a turn on the same session.
4. Show each reply from its saved conversation_turn event: each entry of the turn's cast (its display_name and text) in its own bubble under that name, and the Coach's note (the turn's coach.text) in a separate panel labeled Coach (show nothing when coach is null or empty). With the reply, show the safety status (its level and response action) apart from the conversation, and the receipt: the request id, the turns billed and the charge.
5. Beside each character's line, show a face for that character from the saved turn's characters (match each to its line by speaker_id, and use its expression_group): a face drawn in code for each of the five expression_group moods, and a neutral face when it is empty. Keep all the face artwork in one clearly named file, with one entry per mood and a comment that says how to put in your own images instead of the drawn ones.
6. Treat a turn as complete only when its done event arrives with the same request id and session id as its metadata event. Then append its receipt as one JSON line to receipts.jsonl on the server: request id, session id, user id, operation, safety level, units, the amount in micro-dollars and the settlement.
7. A package.json whose `npm start` serves the page at http://localhost:$PORT (default 3000), and a README that says how to run it.

Rules:
- Keep the API key on the server, in the FOREVERLEARNING_API_KEY environment variable. Read the API host from FOREVERLEARNING_BASE_URL, and send FOREVERLEARNING_ASSIGNMENT_ID as X-Assignment-Id. Never send the key to the browser, print it or write it into a file.
- Give every POST its own new Idempotency-Key, a UUID. If a turn's outcome is uncertain (the connection ends before done), look it up with GET /v1/requests/<request id>. Never send it again under a new key while its outcome is uncertain.
- If a turn fails (an error event arrives before done), it was not charged and it is final: show a short message in your own words and let the user send a message again. Never show raw error text or JSON.
- Show the characters' words exactly as returned. When a saved turn's structure is "unavailable", show its text without inventing a speaker.
- The faces are the characters' simulated responses in this practice, never a reading of the user. Give each face its mood in words as its accessible label only, never as a caption on the page: the user reads the face.
- Use a pseudonymous user id, never a name or an email. Make a new random id for each new browser; never reuse a fixed test id.
- The opening and each message are billable text turns, at 3¢ per text turn. Test with the opening and two messages, no more, as one user, keeping the same cookie: a key admits only a limited number of new users a day. Don't end the session: closing is a turn too, and the next step covers it.
- Ending is optional: opening the learner's next session closes the open one with one billable closeout (3 cents), the same as calling end yourself. Call end when you want the debrief right away. Do not call end just to start another practice.
- Stop only the processes you started; never stop processes by name.

Done when:
- you ran `npm start`, the page showed the room's opening, you sent a message, and a character answered by name
- a face beside each character's line, and the Coach's note, the safety status and the receipt with the reply, apart from the characters' lines
- receipts.jsonl has one line for each confirmed turn
kits.check:
# Your first practice room: what you should see

> The replies below are quoted word for word from one of our test runs of this kit, an app built from its prompt.

Run `npm start` and open http://localhost:3000.

## The opening

The room opens before you type anything. A character from "Direct Feedback To A Report" speaks first, under their name. The Coach's note sits in its own panel. The opening is a billable text turn, so it has its own receipt.

> **Jon:** You said fifteen minutes. What’s this about?
>
> **Coach**
>
> What happened: Jon asked directly for the purpose of the meeting.
>
> Why it matters: Naming the issue clearly can reduce uncertainty and keep the conversation focused.
>
> Next move: You could briefly state what happened in the Halvorsen handoff and why you need to discuss it.

## Your turn, and the reply

Answer the character. For example:

> I wanted to talk about the last two reports. They came in after the deadline, and I'd like to understand what's getting in the way.

The complete reply comes back to your application, checked before anything is shown:

1. **The character's line,** in their own bubble, under their name. In a room with more than one person, each speaks in their own bubble.
2. **The Coach's note,** in its own panel. The Coach answers with every turn, in English. If the note is empty, the panel shows nothing.

> **Jon:** The deadlines weren't the same situation. Brightline had the data-retention change come in late, and Halvorsen was ready from my end. QA was supposed to catch the schema issue.
>
> **Coach**
>
> What happened: You named two missed deadlines and asked what was getting in the way; Jon separated the reports and explained his view of each one.
>
> Why it matters: The specific framing gave him room to respond to the facts rather than treating both handoffs as identical.
>
> Next move: You could ask what he understood the handoff responsibility to be for each report.

Every reply is written fresh, so yours will use different words. The character should still answer in character, as the person in the room.

## The faces

Beside each character's line, a face drawn in code that follows their mood on that turn: one of five moods, or the neutral face when no expression is reported. The faces are the characters' simulated responses, never a reading of you.

**Your own artwork.** All the face artwork is in one place: in the finished checkpoint, the block marked **YOUR OWN ARTWORK GOES HERE** in `public/faces.js`. Put your images in `public/faces/` and write each one's address there, one per mood (and if you like, per expression or per character). Any mood you leave empty keeps the drawn face.

## The safety status

With each reply: **Safety: clear** and **action: none** for an ordinary practice. The levels a Conversations turn can show are `clear`, `watch` and `critical`, with the action `none` or `support`. `unknown` means the turn was not evaluated, and is never an all-clear. Step 8 shows how your app responds to each.

## The receipt

With each reply, from the turn's final `done` event:

- **1 text turn · $0.03 · settled**: one billable text turn, 3¢.
- **Request: …**: the request id. Keep it: it is how you look a turn up (`GET /v1/requests/<id>`) or ask us about it. Showing a shortened request id is fine if the full id is on the reply too, for example on hover.

In `receipts.jsonl` on your server, one line for each confirmed turn, the opening included. For example:

```json
{"request_id":"…","session_id":"…","user_id":"user-…","operation":"turn","safety_level":"clear","units":1,"amount_micro_usd":30000,"settlement":"settled"}
```

## And one thing you should not see

The key. Open your browser's developer tools: the page calls only your own server, never the Conversations API, and no page or script contains the key.

Goal: a Finish button that closes the practice, and a debrief that shows what happened and what it means, each line linked to the turn it came from.

Read first: https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/conversation-practice/ (the Conversations API integration guide), and the OpenAPI contract and the TypeScript example linked there. Use only what they describe.

Start from: this folder, step 1's practice room.

Build:
1. Give each turn on the page an id made from its ordinal (for example turn-3), so other parts of the page can link to it.
2. A Finish button. On Finish, the server closes the session with POST /v1/sessions/<session id>/end and an operation id it saves with the session first; a retried Finish sends the same operation id. Accept the closeout only when its session_ended event and its done event arrive. Show the closing turn like any other, with its safety status and receipt, and append its receipt to receipts.jsonl.
3. Then read the session's debrief and show it in plain words: what happened, what it means, the key moments with their takeaway and the next thing to try, how each character responded at the start and later, and the next practice. Beside each line, link to the turns its evidence references point to.
4. When the debrief is unavailable, show its reason in a plain sentence of your own, never the code.
5. After Finish, no more turns can be sent in that session.

Rules:
- Keep step 1's faces beside each character's line, and its one place for your own face artwork.
- The key is already in the environment. Never print it or write it into a file, not even a .env file.
- Keep step 1's rules: the key only on the server, a new Idempotency-Key for each POST, a failed turn (final, not charged) in your own words with the user free to send again, the characters' words exactly as returned.
- Describe how the characters responded as simulated responses in this practice, never as a reading of the user.
- The closeout is a billable text turn, at 3¢ per text turn, charged when it is saved; reading the debrief adds no charge. Test with one practice only: the opening, two or three messages and one Finish.
- Ending is optional: opening the learner's next session closes the open one with one billable closeout (3 cents), the same as calling end yourself. Call end when you want the debrief right away. Do not call end just to start another practice.
- Stop only the processes you started; never stop processes by name.

Done when:
- you ran `npm start`, practiced two or three turns, pressed Finish, and the closing turn showed with its receipt
- the debrief shows on the page, and at least one of its links lands on the turn it names
- receipts.jsonl has one line for each confirmed turn, the closeout included

# Close and debrief: what you should see

> The replies and the debrief below are quoted word for word from one of our test runs of this kit, an app built from its prompt. Every reply is written fresh, so yours will use different words.

Run `npm start`, open http://localhost:3000, answer the character two or three times, then press **Finish**.

## The closeout

The character's closing line and the Coach's closing note, shown like any other turn. Under it, the safety status and the receipt: **1 text turn · $0.03**. Showing a shortened request id is fine if the full id is on the reply too, for example on hover. The closeout is a billable text turn, charged when it is saved. After it, the message box goes away: the practice is finished.

> **Jon:** Okay. We can pick this up another time.
>
> **Coach**
>
> Debrief: You used an open question to get Jon to describe the second report, and he provided specific timing, ownership, and process details.
>
> Strength: You kept the exchange focused on the work rather than turning it into a personal accusation.
>
> Growth edge: The next conversation could connect those facts to the impact of the missed handoff and the expectation for future sign-off.
>
> Practice markers: Open question; Clarity and specificity.

The closing turn keeps the faces beside each character's line, as every turn does (see step 1's check for where your own artwork goes).

## Your debrief

Reading the debrief adds no charge. It describes the recorded practice:

- **What happened** and **what it means**, each line with links to the turns it came from. Follow a link and the page scrolls to that turn.
- **Key moments:** a title, the takeaway and the next thing to try.
- **How they responded:** how each character's responses moved, from the start to later. These are simulated responses in this practice, never a reading of you.
- **Your next practice.**
- **From the Coach:** the Coach's closing words.

> **What happened**
>
> At turn 1, the first recorded practice moment included Clarity and specificity and Open question.
>
> At turn 2, the last recorded practice moment included Open question.
>
> **What it means**
>
> Clarity and specificity was recorded as something you practiced in this session.
>
> An open question was recorded as a way of inviting the other person’s response.
>
> **Key moments**
>
> *Clarity and specificity*
>
> Takeaway: The recorded evidence shows Clarity and specificity in this session.
>
> Next thing to try: In another practice, notice what changes when you use Clarity and specificity again.
>
> *Open question*
>
> Takeaway: The recorded evidence shows Open question in this session.
>
> Next thing to try: In another practice, notice what changes when you use Open question again.
>
> **How the characters responded**
>
> These are simulated character responses in this practice, never a reading of you.
>
> At the start, Jon responded more cautiously.
>
> Later, Jon showed more strain.
>
> Later, Jon showed more strain.
>
> **Next practice**
>
> Build on: Clarity and specificity

In your app, each of these lines links to the turns it came from.

Feedback comes at three levels: the Coach in the moment, this debrief after, and Insights across practices (a later step).

## If the debrief isn't there

A practice that is too short may have no debrief. Your app says so in a plain sentence, for example: "This practice was too short for a debrief. Next time, stay with the conversation a few more turns before you finish."

## The receipts

`receipts.jsonl` gains one line for each confirmed turn: the opening, each message and the closeout (`"operation":"closeout"`).

kits.prompt:
Goal: a practice picker. The user chooses a ready-made room and the people in it, or practices on their own topic, then practices as in step 1, with every character's line under that character's own name and face.

Read first: https://developers.foreverlearning.ai/docs/conversation-practice/ (the Conversations API integration guide), and the OpenAPI contract and the TypeScript example linked there. Use only what they describe.

Start from: this folder, step 1's practice room.

Build:
1. A picker page, the first thing a user sees, built from the catalog the server reads: its rooms (title, category_id, description, modes, min_participants, max_participants, recommended_personas, topic_consent_required), its personas (display_name, role), its categories and its modes (each with a label). Use plain form controls with visible labels, so the picker works from the keyboard and with a screen reader:
   - Radio buttons labeled "A ready-made room" and "Open practice", the first chosen.
   - For a room: a select labeled Room, listing every room whose topic_consent_required is false by its title, grouped under its category's label (rooms that need topic consent come in a later step). Show the chosen room's description. Never show a room id.
   - A select labeled Mode: the chosen room's modes, by the catalog's labels, with guided chosen.
   - A checkbox for each persona, labeled with the persona's display_name and role. Choosing a room ticks its recommended_personas, and the user may change who is ticked. Say the room's limit in words (for example "This room seats 1 to 2 people"), and allow a start only with min_participants to max_participants people ticked.
   - For open practice: a text box labeled Topic (optional, up to 240 characters), radio buttons labeled "One-on-one" (exactly one person) and "A room" (two to five people), and the same person checkboxes, none ticked to begin with.
   - A button labeled Start practice.
2. On Start practice, the server checks the same limits, then prepares one session for the user. For a room: setup kind "room", its room_id, the mode, and the ticked people as participants, each by persona_id. For open practice: setup kind "open", mode "open_practice", cast_shape "one_on_one" or "room", the ticked people as participants, and the topic. Then it requests that session's opening once. If the API refuses the setup, show a short message in your own words and keep the picker as it was: preparing a session adds no charge.
3. The practice page, as in step 1: the room's title (or "Open practice" and the topic), the names of the people in it, the opening, and each message the user sends as a turn on that session. Show each entry of each turn's cast under its own display_name in its own bubble, with that speaker's face (match the saved turn's characters to the line by speaker_id). With several people, more than one may answer in a turn. Keep step 1's Coach panel, safety status, receipt, faces file and receipts.jsonl.
4. A button labeled New practice that goes back to the picker. A new choice prepares a new session. Do not end the earlier session yourself: opening the new one closes it with one billable closeout (3 cents).

Rules:
- Keep the API key on the server, in the FOREVERLEARNING_API_KEY environment variable. Read the API host from FOREVERLEARNING_BASE_URL, and send FOREVERLEARNING_ASSIGNMENT_ID as X-Assignment-Id. Never send the key to the browser, print it or write it into a file.
- Give every POST its own new Idempotency-Key, a UUID. If a turn's outcome is uncertain (the connection ends before done), look it up with GET /v1/requests/<request id>. Never send it again under a new key while its outcome is uncertain.
- If a turn fails (an error event arrives before done), it was not charged and it is final: show a short message in your own words and let the user send a message again. Never show raw error text or JSON.
- An error status instead of an event stream means the turn was not committed or charged. Let the user send it again; the server sends it with a new Idempotency-Key.
- Show the characters' words exactly as returned. When a saved turn's structure is "unavailable", show its text without inventing a speaker.
- The faces are the characters' simulated responses in this practice, never a reading of the user. Give each face its mood in words as its accessible label only, never as a caption on the page: the user reads the face.
- Use a pseudonymous user id, never a name or an email. Make a new random id for each new browser; never reuse a fixed test id.
- Preparing a session adds no charge. The opening and each message are billable text turns, at 3¢ per text turn, however many people are in the room. Test as one user: test through a browser, or keep one cookie jar across your requests, so every request carries the same cookie. Test two practices, no more: "Direct Feedback To A Report" with its recommended people (the opening and one message), and a practice with two or more people you chose (the opening and one message). Don't end a session: closing is a turn too.
- Ending is optional: opening the learner's next session closes the open one with one billable closeout (3 cents), the same as calling end yourself. Call end when you want the debrief right away. Do not call end just to start another practice.
- Stop only the processes you started; never stop processes by name.

Done when:
- you ran `npm start`, picked a room, and its opening showed with each speaker's name and face
- you chose your own people for a practice, and the people you chose answered, each under their own name
- the Coach's note, the safety status and the receipt show with each reply, and receipts.jsonl has one line for each confirmed turn

# Pick the room and the cast: what you should see

> The replies below are quoted word for word from one of our test runs of this kit, an app built from its prompt. Every reply is written fresh, so yours will use different words.

Run `npm start` and open http://localhost:3000.

## The picker

The picker comes first. Every ready-made room that needs no topic consent is in the **Room** list, grouped by category, with its description. (Rooms that ask for topic consent come in a later step.) Under it:

- **Mode:** the room's modes, with guided practice chosen.
- **The people:** a checkbox for every character, by name and role. Choosing a room ticks the people it recommends. Untick them and tick others if you like: anyone can join any room, as long as the room's limit holds. The page says the limit in words, for example "This room seats 1 to 2 people".
- **Open practice:** your own topic (up to 240 characters), one-on-one with one person or a room of two to five.

Tick more people than the room seats and press **Start practice**: the practice doesn't start, and the page says why in plain words. Preparing a session adds no charge, so a refused start costs nothing.

## A room with several people

Pick "Direct Feedback To A Report" and press **Start practice**. The room opens with the people you chose. With more than one person in the room, more than one may answer in a turn, each in their own bubble, under their own name, with their own face.

## Your own people

Press **New practice**, pick a room, tick your own people and start. The people you ticked are the people in the room: they are the ones who answer.

For example, open practice as a room with Dana and Noor, on the topic "Agreeing on who presents the quarterly results at Friday's meeting." Both answer in each turn:

> **Dana:** Look, Friday's meeting is in three days, and I'm not presenting the quarterly results for the team again. We need one person owning that deck and the questions that come with it.
>
> **Noor:** I can take part of it. I have been tracking the open threads, so I could handle the results summary if that helps. I just do not want us deciding this in a way that leaves the handoff unclear.
>
> **Coach**
>
> What happened: Dana set a firm boundary around presenting, while Noor offered partial help and raised the need for a clear handoff.
>
> Why it matters: The room has two workable starting points, but ownership and scope are still open.
>
> Next move: You could name who should own the presentation and ask what support would make that handoff workable.
>
> **You:** I'd like to present the results this time. How should we split it?
>
> **Dana:** You present the results. Noor, you take the open questions and track anything we cannot answer on the spot. I will handle the overall narrative and step in if the room gets stuck.
>
> **Noor:** That works for me. I can keep the question list tight and flag anything that needs a follow-up before Friday.
>
> **Coach**
>
> What happened: You offered to present the results, and Dana assigned Noor the open questions while keeping the overall narrative.
>
> Why it matters: The split gives each person a defined part and leaves a clear backup for questions that need follow-up.
>
> Next move: You could confirm who will prepare the question list and when you will review the deck together.

## With each reply

As in step 1: the Coach's note in its own panel, the safety status (for example `Safety: clear · action: none`) and the receipt (`1 text turn · $0.03` and the request id). Showing a shortened request id is fine if the full id is on the reply too, for example on hover. A room of five costs the same per turn as a room of one: 3¢ per text turn.

## The faces

Beside each character's line, a face drawn in code that follows their mood on that turn: one of five moods, or the neutral face when no expression is reported. The faces are the characters' simulated responses, never a reading of you.

**Your own artwork.** All the face artwork is in one place: in the finished checkpoint, the block marked **YOUR OWN ARTWORK GOES HERE** in `public/faces.js`. Put your images in `public/faces/` and write each one's address there, one per mood (and if you like, per expression or per character). Any mood you leave empty keeps the drawn face.

## If a message doesn't go through

If the API answers with an error instead of the reply, the turn was not committed or charged. The page says so in plain words and you can send it again; your server sends it as a new request.

## The receipts

`receipts.jsonl` gains one line for each confirmed turn: each opening and each message.

> **Riley:** Hey. Let’s get straight to the project story. Give me the version you’d use in the interview: what was going wrong, what did you do, and what changed?
>
> **Coach**
>
> What happened: Riley opened with the three parts the interview story needs: the problem, your action, and the result.
>
> Why it matters: A clear sequence will keep the example specific without letting it sprawl.
>
> Next move: You could start with the project problem and include one concrete sign that it was going off track.
>
> **You:** Thanks for having me. I've spent four years leading a small support team, and I'm looking to move into operations.
>
> **Riley:** That gives me the direction, but not the story yet. Pick one project that had a clear problem, and walk me through your role, the action you took, and the result. Keep the sequence intact.
>
> **Coach**
>
> What happened: You opened with relevant experience and named the role you want, while Riley asked for a specific project example.
>
> Why it matters: The background establishes your direction, but the interview answer still needs one concrete problem and a result.
>
> Next move: You could choose one project and state the problem, your action, and the measurable outcome in that order.

## The faces

Beside each character's line, a face drawn in code that follows their mood on that turn: one of five moods, or the neutral face when no expression is reported. The faces are the characters' simulated responses, never a reading of you.

**Your own artwork.** All the face artwork is in one place: in the finished checkpoint, the block marked **YOUR OWN ARTWORK GOES HERE** in `public/faces.js`. Put your images in `public/faces/` and write each one's address there, one per mood (and if you like, per expression or per character). Any mood you leave empty keeps the drawn face.

## Finish, and your debrief

**Finish** closes the interview: the closing turn, with its receipt. Then your debrief, in plain words: what happened, what it means, the key moments and your next practice. Each line links to the answer it came from. How the interviewer responded is how they were written to respond in this practice, never a reading of you.

> **What happened**
>
> At turn 1, the first recorded moment marked Clarity and specificity as a possible next experiment.
>
> At turn 2, the last recorded practice moment included Collaborative next step; Clarity and specificity was recorded as a possible next experiment.
>
> **What it means**
>
> Clarity and specificity was recorded as a missed opportunity or possible next experiment, not as a judgment about intent.
>
> A collaborative next step was recorded as part of the close.
>
> **Key moments**
>
> Clarity and specificity: The recorded evidence points to Clarity and specificity as a useful experiment.
>
> Collaborative next step: The recorded evidence shows Collaborative next step in this session.
>
> **Next practice**
>
> In another practice, deliberately try Clarity and specificity.
>
> In another practice, notice what changes when you use Collaborative next step again.

In your app, each of these lines links to the answers it came from.

If the interview was too short for a debrief, a plain sentence says so.

## Practice again

**Practice again** starts round 2 with the same challenge. **Practice again, harder** sets the challenge to resistant: the interviewer holds their position and makes you earn any movement. Once there is an earlier interview to compare with, the next debrief shows what was new this time.

## The receipts

`receipts.jsonl` gains one line for each confirmed turn: each opening, each answer and each closeout. One full interview of three answers is five billable text turns, 15¢.

| --- | --- |

# Step 3: Pick the room and the cast

Step 1's practice room, plus a picker. The user chooses a ready-made room and the people in it, or practices on their own topic, then practices as in step 1, with every character's line under that character's own name and face. Your server keeps the key; the page talks only to your server.

## You need

- A developer workspace with the Conversations API added, and a server key from **My APIs**.
- Node 24 or later. No packages to install.

## Run it

```sh
cp .env.example .env        # then put your key and assignment id in .env
npm start
```

Open http://localhost:3000. The picker opens on **A ready-made room**, with "Direct Feedback To A Report" and its recommended people ticked. Press **Start practice**, then answer, for example "I wanted to talk about the last two reports. They came in after the deadline, and I'd like to understand what's getting in the way."

Then press **New practice**, pick a room, tick your own people, and answer again. Or choose **Open practice**, give a topic if you like, choose **One-on-one** (one person) or **A room** (two to five people), and tick the people.

## What you should see

- The picker: **Room** lists every room by its title, grouped under its category. The room's description, its **Mode** (guided first), and a checkbox for every person, by name and role. Choosing a room ticks its recommended people; anyone may join any room, within its seats. The picker says the limit in words, for example "This room seats 1 to 2 people."
- A start refused, in plain words, when the people ticked are outside the limit. If the Conversations API refuses a setup, a short message, and the picker stays as it was.
- The practice: the room's title (or "Open practice" and the topic), the names of the people in it, and the opening.
- Each speaker's line under their own name, with their face beside it. With several people in the room, more than one may answer in a turn.
- With each reply, the Coach's note in its own panel, the safety status and the receipt: `1 text turn · $0.03 · settled` and the request id.
- A new line in `receipts.jsonl` for each confirmed turn, each opening included.

## How it works

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `server.ts` | Serves the page and gives each new browser a pseudonymous user id in a cookie. `/api/state` reads the catalog (no charge) and sends the picker: rooms that need no topic consent, by title and category, the people, the modes by label. `/api/start` checks the choice against the same limits, prepares one session (no charge) and requests its opening, once. `/api/turn` relays each message as a turn. `/api/new` goes back to the picker; it does not end the earlier session. Opening the next session closes the open one with one billable closeout (3 cents). |
| `conversations.ts` | Step 1's client, plus the catalog's categories and modes, and `prepareOpen` for open practice next to `prepareRoom`. An error that the API itself reports (an error status, or an error event before `done`) is marked as not committed. |
| `public/` | The picker and the practice page. Each reply shows every character's line under their name, with the face that matches the line's speaker, the Coach in its own panel, and the safety status and receipt apart from the conversation. |
